Five of those six times marked the exact bottom

• 1987: Black Monday capitulation low 
• 1998: The literal bottom tick of the LTCM crisis 
• 2002: The terminal flush of the dot-com bust 
• 2008: The only failure (full banking system insolvency) • 2011: The cycle low before an eight-year bull run 
• 2020: The generational COVID liquidation wick

Friday was the seventh.

The only time buying a 40 VIX failed was 2008, when the global banking system froze. Every other time, it was the trade of the year.

$AIL and $ANS, leveraged ETFs on $ANT, are expected to launch at the open.

Worth understanding the risks as these ETFs are mainly short term trading vehicles. $AIL seeks 2x the daily move of $ANT and $ANS seeks -2x.

So if $ANT closes up 5%, $AIL aims for +10% and $ANS aims for -10%. A down day flips that.

The key word is daily. Both funds reset at the close and start fresh the next session. Because of that reset, returns over weeks or months won't equal 2x the stock. Say $ANT jumps 5% one day and falls right back the next. The stock is flat, yet both funds finish slightly down.

That's why the prospectus calls them short term trading vehicles for people who actively watch their positions.

The 2-year US inflation swap just closed at 2.09%. A few weeks ago it was near 2.65%. Bond traders took more than half a point off their inflation forecast for the next two years in about a month.

For scale, this same swap peaked at 4.84% in March 2022, when the market thought inflation was out of control. The six-year average is 2.74%. Today we sit 65 bps below that average, and closer to the 2020 lows than to the 2022 panic.

The Fed's 2% target is for PCE, and this swap tracks CPI, which has historically run a few tenths hotter. 

So a 2.09% CPI swap means the bond market expects the Fed to be at its target, or a little under it.

Once inflation stops being the excuse, rates MUST come down. A lower discount rate helps most where the cash flows are furthest out: semis, software, and every company in the AI buildout that's still spending today for earnings in 2028.

最近研究了一家比较有意思的美股公司，$OPNW（OpenWorld）。@openworld_HQ

我一直有个观点：RWA 下一阶段真正值得关注的，不是把多少资产搬到链上，而是谁能解决传统金融市场真实存在的融资需求。

OPNW 就是一个值得研究的案例。

1. 公司背景

OPNW 今年 10 月正式以新代码在 Nasdaq 交易，主要通过 OpenWorld Enterprise 为企业提供资产代币化、融资结构设计和技术服务。

团队有一定传统金融背景。CEO Matthew Shaw 曾任职 UBS，也创立过加密资产管理公司 Protos；Russel McMeekin 则有 Honeywell 的企业技术管理经验。

2. AI CapEx 的二阶传导，可能是 RWA 的新机会
我之前反复讲过，AI CapEx 的二阶增速不可能永远加速。
未来市场关注的重点，会逐渐从算力投入规模转向资本效率、融资成本和资产回报率。

OPNW 目前推进的两个项目恰好切中了这个方向：

Meridian：拟通过上限 10 亿美元的代币化融资，建设光伏、储能支持的分布式 AI 算力网络。

BeyondAI：拟以知识产权作为抵押品，进行上限 1.3 亿美元的代币化融资。

两个项目都不能直接视为已完成融资或已确认收入。

但我认为背后的逻辑值得关注：当 AI 企业开始更加重视资本效率，知识产权、算力设备、能源资产等，都可能成为新的融资标的。

RWA 的机会可能不只在国债和传统信贷。

3. Solana 生态的参与

11 月 10 日，代币化 OPNW 上线 Solana，由 Backpack Securities 发行。

Solana 官方账号进行了相关直播，Frontier Traders 也推出了 OPNW 交易奖励活动。

我更关注的是，传统上市公司的股票开始获得新的链上交易渠道。这不等于 Solana 对股价背书，但确实让 OPNW 获得了一定的生态曝光。

4. 估值差距与我的研究框架

按照 11 月 16 日收盘市值及 Q3 收入年化口径计算：
Securitize：16.1x P/S
Figure：5.0x P/S
OPNW：0.28x P/S

OPNW 当时市值约 835 万美元，Q3 收入约 740 万美元。
估值倍数差距确实很大，但我不认为简单套用同行估值，就能证明公司被低估。

尤其 OPNW Q3 约 89% 的收入来自关联方，相关 RWA 收入截至季末尚未开票或回款，收入质量仍然需要验证。

按照我的研究框架，接下来主要关注三个变量：

宏观流动性：利率和融资环境是否支持项目交割？
现金流兑现：项目能否从融资意向变成实际收入和回款？
估值预期差：第三方客户增长、收入质量改善，能否支撑市场重新定价？

——————————————

我认为 AI CapEx 周期的下一阶段，不只是半导体和数据中心之间的利润重新分配，也可能带来融资结构和资本市场服务的新需求。

OPNW 正好处在 RWA 与 AI 资产融资的交叉点上。

This is the most important post you'll ever see. 

The biggest question I get is what happens if you bought the top of individual stocks that may never recover.

Here's how to recover, the professional way:

1. Tax Loss Harvesting (do this first)

This is the single most valuable move you can make right now. The IRS lets you use investment losses to offset gains and reduce your tax bill.

How it works:
- Sell your losing positions to realize the loss on paper
- Use those losses to offset any capital gains you had this year (from other trades, crypto, real estate, etc.)
- If your losses exceed your gains, you can deduct up to $3,000 per year against ordinary income
- Any remaining losses carry forward indefinitely to future tax years

The swap trick:
- For example, sell $NBIS at a 70% loss, book the loss
- Immediately buy a similar but not "substantially identical" stock (this avoids the wash sale rule)
- Example: sell one AI infrastructure name, buy another. Sell $SMCI, buy $DELL. Sell $NBIS, buy an AI ETF. You stay exposed to the same theme but you banked the tax loss.
- The wash sale rule says you cannot buy the same or substantially identical security within 30 days before or after the sale. Different companies in the same sector are fine.

The math:
- You put $50K into AI stocks, now worth $15K. That is a $35K realized loss if you sell.
- If you had $20K in gains elsewhere this year, that $35K loss wipes out the $20K in gains (saving you roughly $3,000 to $7,000 in taxes depending on your bracket)
- The remaining $15K loss carries forward. $3K offsets income this year, $3K next year, $3K the year after, and so on.
- You are literally getting paid by the government to reposition your portfolio.

Deadline: You must sell BEFORE December 31 to claim the loss for this tax year. Do not wait.

2. The Quality Audit

Pull up every position and sort them into three buckets:

Bucket A: Leaders with real earnings - $NVDA, $MSFT, $GOOGL, $META, $AMZN, $ORCL, $TSM
- These are down 30 to 50% but they print cash, have massive moats, and will recover
- Action: hold, or add slowly if you have capital

Bucket B: Promising but speculative- companies with real revenue growing fast but no sustained profitability yet
- Action: trim to a size where you can sleep at night. If it goes to zero tomorrow, it should not change your life.

Bucket C: Hopes and dreams - pre-revenue, story stocks, SPACs, names down 70%+ with no clear path to profitability
- Action: tax loss harvest these immediately. Sell, book the loss, move on. These are the ones that may never come back. Down 70% can easily become down 95%.

3. The Rebalancing Framework

You said you put "all your money" in AI stocks. That is the real problem, not the drawdown. Concentration killed you, not the thesis.

Target allocation going forward:
- 55% core holdings (strongest fundamental leaders or blue chip leaders)
- 30% high conviction sector bets (AI infrastructure, semis, cloud)
- 15% growth and speculative (the ones you believe in long term)

How to get there from here:
- Use the tax loss harvest proceeds to buy broad index exposure
- You are not "giving up" on AI. You are building a base that lets you survive the volatility without panicking.

4. The Dollar Cost Average Recovery

If you believe in AI long term (and you should, the capex cycle is real), set up a systematic plan:

- Take whatever new capital you can invest each month
- Split it: 60% into stronger fundamental names, 40% into your highest conviction AI name
- Do this every single month regardless of what the market does
- In 12 to 24 months, your average cost basis will be dramatically lower than your original buy

This is how you turn a bad entry into a good position over time. You are not "averaging down" emotionally. You are executing a plan.

5. The Covered Call Income Strategy

If you hold 100+ shares of any position, you can sell covered calls against them to generate income while you wait for recovery.

How it works:
- You own 100 shares of $NVDA at $140 (bought at $200)
- Sell a call option at $170 strike, 30 to 45 days out, collect $400 to $800 in premium
- If NVDA stays below $170, you keep the premium and your shares. Repeat monthly.
- If NVDA goes above $170, your shares get called away at $170 (you still made $30/share from your current price plus the premium)

The math over a year:
- Collecting $500/month in premium on a $14,000 position is roughly 40% annualized income
- This dramatically accelerates your breakeven timeline even if the stock goes sideways

6. The Roth Conversion Play

If your portfolio is down 70%, this is actually the best time to do a Roth conversion.

- Convert your beaten down AI stocks from a Traditional IRA to a Roth IRA
- You pay taxes on the current (low) value, not the original value
- When those stocks recover (and if they are quality names, they will), all the gains are tax free forever
- You are essentially converting $15K worth of stock that you originally paid $50K for. You pay tax on $15K now instead of $50K+ later.

7. The Mental Framework

Stop thinking about your entry price. It is irrelevant. The market does not know or care what you paid.

The only question that matters every single day: "If I had cash instead of this position right now, would I buy it
today at this price?"

- If yes, hold.
- If no, sell and redeploy into something you would buy.
- If maybe, trim to a smaller size.

Your portfolio should only contain positions you would actively choose to own today. Anything you are holding just because you are "waiting to get back to even" is a position you should probably exit.

The Action Plan (this week)

1. Today: List every position, current value, and loss amount
2. This week: Sort into Bucket A, B, and C
3. Before Dec 31: Tax loss harvest all Bucket C names. Swap into similar exposure or broad index.
4. January: Set up the monthly DCA plan. Start the covered call strategy on your largest positions.
5. Ongoing: Stop checking daily. Set a calendar reminder to review quarterly.
